history.summary: The Maruti Temple (Shri Marutirai Sansthan) stands on Altinho Hill overlooking Fontainhas in Panjim (Panaji), dedicated to Lord Hanuman. Local lore, repeated across travel sources, says the Hanuman idol was kept hidden here during the Portuguese colonial era when Hindu temples were destroyed, and devotees worshipped secretly at the spot until the end of Portuguese rule. CONFLICT (verify): one account dates the present shrine's construction to 1931–1934, while most sources say the visible temple was built after Goa's liberation in 1961; origins in the Kadamba dynasty (10th–14th century) are also claimed but unsupported. The bright orange-facaded temple is lit at night and visible from afar; the main idol can be glimpsed from the main road through an opening in the basement wall, and a natural freshwater spring with three tanks at the foothill serves the local community. Coordinates are approximate (locality-level, verify).

name: Maruti Temple
town_description: Panaji (Panjim) is the capital city of Goa, set on the southern bank of the Mandovi River estuary in North Goa district. It became the Portuguese capital of Goa in 1843 and retains a colonial character in its Latin Quarter of Fontainhas, while Altinho Hill hosts the archbishop's palace and state government buildings. It is the state's administrative and cultural centre and the main gateway for North Goa tourism.
